candidates.title: LIMITATIONS
candidates.description:
When an employee approach his supervisor to have some request, and the supervisor will tell him that he is not in the position to grant his request, and points out that it is the manager's position to grant his request, this means that he is accepting his limitations.

But, when the supervisor in fact has the capacity to grant the request of the employee and said he can't grant, he is deceitful.

This is what happened to Jesus Christ when a certain mother approached him for a request.

Open your Bible at Mat 20:20-23 it says:

Then the mother of the sons of Zeb′e·dee approached him with her sons, doing obeisance and asking for something from him.  He said to her: “What do you want?” She said to him: “Give the word that these my two sons may sit down, one at your right hand and one at your left, in your kingdom.”  Jesus said in answer: “YOU men do not know what YOU are asking for. Can YOU drink the cup that I am about to drink?” They said to him: “We can.”  He said to them: “YOU will indeed drink my cup, but this sitting down at my right hand and at my left is not mine to give, but it belongs to those for whom it has been prepared by my Father.

This account proves to be a good point to reason out that Jesus is not the Almighty God. If Jesus was actually God that came down to earth, then he can grant the request of the mother.
candidates.creator: whologwhy

candidates.title: LAI GARDEN
candidates.description:
Dining at Lai Garden at SM City Cebu. Love the foods here, number one the foods are tasty but not salty. The price is affordable and sulit for your money. The service is fast and friendly.

We tried their combo meal good for 5 persons for only P499.00. This includes Fried Chicken (half) 4 pcs Siomai, 1 platter of flat noodles, 10 pcs. Lumpia Shanghai, 5 cups of Rice, and 5 glass of Iced Tea.

I will recommend this to my friends here when you have time in Cebu. Visit Lai Garden, located at the North Wing Atrium, in between Chikaan sa Cebu and Bigbys.

Lola Saling's Seafoods is located at Casuntingan, Mandaue City.

Here you can order, Fish Tinola, Grilled Fish, Squid, Tangigue (Spanish Mackerel) Green Caviar (Lato) Lechon Native Chicken.

I love the surroundings with so many herbs planted. You can have the fresh pepper (siling kulikot) Basil Leaves, Sangig, Tanglad(Lemon Grass) Parsely and many more herbs.

candidates.title: File:The abaca footwear from Bantayan Island, Cebu 1.jpg
candidates.creator: Bim24
candidates.description:
The abaca footwear from Bantayan Island, Cebu is a traditional Filipino craft made from abaca fibers, known for their durability and comfort. These abaca slippers are also displayed at The Kabilin Center, showcasing the artistry and craftsmanship of local artisans.
The Bantayan Ladies Strand Association from Bantayan Island produces handmade abaca slippers, which can also be seen in the exhibits at The Kabilin Center. These products symbolize the cultural heritage of the region. The artisans from Bantayan Island carefully create each pair with dedication to their craft.

If you are interested in purchasing abaca footwear, The Kabilin Center is a great place to view and support local products and artisans.

candidates.title: File:Tagaktak Pasalubong Products.jpg
candidates.creator: Bim24
candidates.description:
Tagaktak is a popular pasalubong treat from Cebu, known for its crispy texture and sweet taste. It is made from a mixture of rice flour, sugar, and coconut, then fried to a golden crisp. The unique feature of Tagaktak is its shape, which resembles little pieces that "sprinkle" or "fall" as they are fried, hence the name.
Tagaktak is usually sold in small bags, perfect for taking home as a souvenir. It’s often paired with other Cebu delicacies like dried mangoes, otap, or chicharon, making it a great addition to any pasalubong collection during Sinulog or other festivals.

candidates.title: File:Handurawang Kinamot.jpg
candidates.creator: Bim24
candidates.description:
"Handurawang Kinamot: Cebuano Design and Heritage" is an exhibit held at The Kabilin Center in Cebu City, celebrating the rich artistry and culture of Cebuano artisans. The exhibit showcases the fusion of traditional designs with modern approaches, highlighting the skills of local artisans whose craft has been passed down through generations.
The exhibit runs until February 7, 2025, and is open to the public from Monday to Saturday, 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM. The entrance fee is Php 150 - 200 per person.
"Handurawang Kinamot" offers a unique opportunity to experience Cebuano culture through its artistic heritage and to see the works of local artisans who embody the traditions of the region.

For more information, you can visit the official website of The Kabilin Center or check their social media pages.

candidates.title: File:Haligi nga makita sa Casa Gorordo.jpg
candidates.creator: Bim24
candidates.description:
Haligi
These are old house posts that were replaced during rehabilitation of the structure. Locally they are known as haligi. Houses like Casa Gorordo used different types of hardwoods for structural support. The most commonly used was molave which is known locally as tugas. Cebu’s limited forests had some of the best types woods, which were decimated quickly in the 19th century when a construction boom esulted from the opening of the province’s economy to world trade.
candidates.categories: Self-published work|Collections of Casa Gorordo

They traveled to the island of Negros at the invitation of the Bishop of Jaro to help provide education to the youth, leading to the eventual opening of St. Paul College (now St. Paul University Dumaguete).
